items.title: Yusef Lateef — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I would over at the other, at the first alto saxophone, John Brown... the third alto player, John Brown, first

ctx.x: ...and I think, I think your comments bear that out. I want to go forward and get back to your work with Kenny Burrell, but before that if you could talk a bit more about uh the Dizzy Gillespie ensemble, because it...fortunately, I think people are beginning to uh to recognize the importance of, well, not just his career, but that, that band. But uh what was that like for you working there, and, and what can you tell us about the importance of that, that big band?

Uh okay, um that was a learning experience for me. Uh for example...uh maybe the first two weeks I was in the band, we would play arrangements like Swedish Suite, Jump Did-Le Ba, and...I would, I would get to an end of a phrase in, in the saxophone section, and like the last note say is a whole note, I’d hold it four beats, and uh then there was a rest, but I noticed the saxophone players were still playing. So, I thought my part was wrong, and so I would over at the other, at the first alto saxophone, John…
